claims.text: At stage-3 NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents handles OrderPlaced, OrderCancelled, OrderShipped (lines 15-19) and three refund events, each by calling outbox.Add with a routing key and an OrderMessage(order id, customer email, name, OccurredAt) (line 34); it never references RabbitMQ or saves.
At stage-3 OrderService calls events.DispatchAsync(order) before repository.SaveChangesAsync() in each use case, so handlers add their rows before the single save.

EfOutbox.Add only adds an OutboxMessage (routing key, JSON body via JsonSerializer.Serialize) to the injected DonHangDbContext; the class has no SaveChangesAsync call. JsonSerializerOptions.Web uses camelCase property names.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Infrastructure/EfOutbox.cs:7-22; .NET docs: JsonSerializerOptions.Web (web defaults: JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase)

claims.text: By default, when the provider supports transactions, EF Core applies all changes of a single SaveChanges/SaveChangesAsync call in one database transaction: if any change fails, none is applied.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Saving Data > Transactions (default transaction behavior)

claims.text: OutboxMessage.Id defaults to Guid.NewGuid(); PublishedAt is nullable and empty until set. DonHangDbContext maps OutboxMessage to table outbox_messages with columns id, routing_key, body (jsonb), created_at, published_at, trace_parent.

Ordering's tables, outbox_messages included, live in the PostgreSQL database donhang; Notifications has its own database and receives order events only through RabbitMQ, via the queue notifications.order-events.
If AddMessage throws (customer not found, line 33), DispatchAsync throws and the use case stops before SaveChangesAsync, so neither the order's change nor any outbox row is saved.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents.cs:32-33; OrderService.cs:43-50 (comment 'A handler that throws stops it here')

claims.text: Two SaveChangesAsync calls with no transaction opened around them (as in Đơn Hàng) are two transactions; if the process stops after the first commits, the order is stored and the outbox row is not.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Saving Data > Transactions (default behavior; controlling transactions via DbContext.Database)

claims.text: Saving the outbox row does not publish it: published_at stays empty and the API answers the request without waiting for RabbitMQ; a separate, later step (OutboxRelay) publishes rows.
At stage-2, QueuedNotifier adds a pending notifications row to the order's DbContext, saved by the same SaveChangesAsync, and NotificationSender sends it later.
At stage-3 RabbitMQ holds queues such as notifications.order-events; no outbox is among RabbitMQ's queues, since outbox_messages lives in PostgreSQL.

claims.text: Keeping the message in a table is what lets the publishing step be retried: the message is stored rather than held in one request's memory.
claims.source_hint: design rationale of the transactional outbox; prereq backend.l3.dual-write

claims.text: DonHangDbContext is registered with AddDbContext (scoped) and EfOutbox with AddScoped, so within one request EfOutbox and the order repository share one DonHangDbContext.
